prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single ORIGINAL medieval RPG dialogue portrait, eventually delivered at 74 x 100 logical pixels. Redraw the supplied identity from scratch in the chunky hard-edged pixel language of the four supplied style references; this is not a resized full-body picture.
Input roles: image 1 is the identity master for facial structure, haircut and recognizable identity ONLY; images 2-5 are style references (Mara, Iwo, Leiya, Tore), NOT subjects to copy. Face proportions are adult and anatomically believable. No chibi, no baby face.
Composition: an extremely tightly framed HEAD portrait on a 74:100 portrait-ratio canvas. Crown nearly reaches the top. Face with strong cheekbones, nose wings and adult jaw fills most of the canvas width and height. Angle gently toward viewer-left. Chin near the bottom; very short neck and only a NARROW strip of specified collar at the bottom, absolutely no chest, torso, hands, props or broad shoulders. Do not surround a small head with empty space.
Style: visibly chunky, hard-edged pixel clusters with crisp stair steps, warm near-black contour. Large coherent shadow/highlight planes describe nose wings, cheekbones and jaw. Small deep-set adult eyes; eye whites are tiny LOW-BRIGHTNESS muted ochre-gray slivers, never white blocks, no eye sparkle. Hair organized into 4-6 solid connected masses with broad stepped lighting, no parallel thin strands, no noisy hatch lines. Work as if designing directly on a 74x100 logical grid, with broad 2-8 pixel clusters, not fine pixel-textured illustration. Matte earth colors, temporary palette at most 32 colors. No smooth gradients, antialiasing, blur, dithering, microtexture, pores, glossy rim light, tiny isolated specks or stray edge fragments. Pixel art with structural planar shading, not a painterly filter.
Backdrop: true transparent alpha outside the silhouette. Single isolated portrait, no words, logo, panels, decorative frame, ground, atmosphere or backdrop. Do not reuse the references' worried facial expression by default; use the individual expression below.

Subject identity: HERLIN / 赫林 / BRY-NPC-HERLIN, a male working rivet repairer around forty. Preserve the lean long adult face, angular cheeks, pronounced rather long nose, short tousled salt-and-pepper charcoal hair and close dark-gray stubble of identity image 1. Dark straight brows, slight under-eye tiredness and a modest uneven closed mouth. His expression is alert and guarded, with quiet dignity: a cautious lateral glance, low relatively level brow rather than high inward worried arches, lips held flat; neither generic sadness, anger nor villain smirk. He is a tradesman under strain, not an old man, noble, soldier, or labor-leader symbol. Keep a small old notch in HIS LEFT ear, the visible ear on viewer-right in this angle, as a subtle silhouette detail with no blood or new wound.
Costume correction: latest written character card overrides the old identity image's rusty-red shirt. Show only a VERY NARROW washed BLUE-GRAY shirt collar and a small worn BROWN LEATHER apron strap/top edge at the very bottom. No red shirt. The apron is practical patched leather; do not turn it into armor or add rank symbols. His small rivet hammer, tin box, hands, apron body and scorch holes stay outside the tight head crop. The face and hair carry the portrait.
